idiom_name: java.lang.reflect.Proxy.newProxyInstance + InvocationHandler with a volatile revocation flag
implementation_notes: The forwarder is a JDK dynamic proxy: Proxy.newProxyInstance(loader, new Class<?>[]{Session.class}, handler) returns an object that implements the interface and dispatches every interface method - plus equals, hashCode and toString - to InvocationHandler.invoke, which is the single check point for the grant. Revocation is a volatile (or AtomicBoolean) flag in the handler that makes invoke throw instead of dispatching, and the proxy class is final, so the collaborator cannot subclass around the gate. Because the interface declares its checked exceptions, prefer an unchecked revocation exception: a checked exception that the proxied method does not declare surfaces at the call site as UndeclaredThrowableException.
pitfalls: A checked exception thrown from invoke that the proxied method does not declare is wrapped in UndeclaredThrowableException (with duplicate method names only the exceptions declared by every proxy interface are allowed), so a checked revocation exception reaches callers as an unexpected type.
equals, hashCode and toString are dispatched to the handler like interface methods, so identity and hashing change at the boundary unless the handler deliberately delegates them to the target.
A non-volatile boolean is not guaranteed to be seen by calling threads - the JIT may hoist the read out of the loop - so the flag must be volatile or atomic.
